em-01:
Dear Professor Lin,

I am writing to explain why I missed last Thursday's biology lab on enzyme activity. On Wednesday night, I developed a fever of nearly 39 degrees, and the next morning I went to the campus health center. The doctor told me to rest for two days and avoid contact with others, so I could not attend. I have a note from the health center that I can bring to class.

Since the lab counts toward our final grade, I would really like to make up the work before the next exam. Would it be possible for me to complete the experiment during another section's lab, or to do an alternative assignment if that is easier?

I am available on Monday and Wednesday afternoons after 1 p.m., and I could also come in on Friday morning. I am happy to adjust my schedule to whatever works best for you or the lab assistant.

Thank you very much for your understanding.

Sincerely,
Anna
em-02:
Dear Ms. Patel,

I am writing about a problem in my apartment, Unit 4B. For the past two weeks, the kitchen faucet has been dripping constantly, even when the handle is turned off completely. I mentioned it to the maintenance worker, Mr. Hill, about ten days ago, but no one has come to repair it yet.

The dripping has become quite disruptive. Because my bedroom is right next to the kitchen, the sound keeps me awake at night, and I have been getting only five or six hours of sleep before my morning classes. I am also concerned about wasting water, so I have been placing a bowl under the faucet and emptying it several times a day.

Could you please let me know when the faucet can be repaired? I am usually home after 4 p.m. on weekdays, but maintenance is welcome to enter while I am out if that is more convenient.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Michael
em-03:
Hi Jordan,

I hope you're doing well! I joined the photography club this semester, and I've really been enjoying it. The weekly photo challenges push me to try new techniques, and last week's workshop on night photography was fantastic. Everyone is so supportive, too.

I wanted to share one idea, though. Many of us have a required chemistry lab on Tuesday evenings, so we can't make it to the meetings. In fact, I've talked to at least five other members who have the same conflict. I've already missed three meetings, and I'm worried about falling behind on our projects.

Would you consider moving the meetings to Thursday evenings at 7? As far as I know, very few required labs or classes are held on Thursday nights, so more members could attend. It might also help us attract new members who haven't been able to come so far. We could even send out a quick poll to see which time works best for most people.

Thanks for listening!

Best,
Sophia
em-04:
Dear Mr. Brooks,

I am writing to request some time off next month. My older sister is getting married in Seattle, and I will need to travel there for the wedding and the family events around it. I wanted to let you know early, before you prepare the schedule.

I will be away from Thursday, June 12, through Saturday, June 14, and I will be back at work on Sunday, June 15. During those dates, I am normally scheduled for three morning shifts.

To make things easier, I have already talked to two coworkers. Emily said she could take my Thursday and Friday shifts, and Jason offered to cover Saturday. In return, I would be happy to work some of their shifts later in the month. If you would prefer a different arrangement, I am also willing to pick up extra hours the week before I leave.

Thank you for considering my request.

Best regards,
Tina
em-05:
Dear Mrs. Alvarez,

Thank you so much for watering my plants and collecting my mail while I was visiting my family last week. When I got home, my plants looked healthier than when I left, and you had even stacked my mail neatly on the table. It was such a relief to know everything was in good hands.

To celebrate the end of the semester, I'm hosting a small dinner for the people on our floor this Saturday at 6:30 p.m. I'm planning to cook a few dishes from my home country, including a chicken curry and a mango dessert my grandmother taught me to make. It will be a relaxed evening with about eight guests, some music, and plenty of good conversation.

I would be delighted if you could join us. Please let me know by Friday whether you can come so that I can make sure there is enough food, and tell me if there is anything you don't eat.

Warm regards,
Priyanka
em-06:
Dear Customer Service Team,

I am writing about a problem with my recent order, number 58217, which included a white desk lamp. Unfortunately, the lamp arrived damaged. The round base has a large crack running across it, and a small piece of plastic was loose inside the box. When I plugged the lamp in and pressed the switch, the light would not turn on at all, even after I tried a different bulb and another outlet.

The package was delivered to my dormitory mailroom on Monday, March 3, and I opened it the same evening. That means I am still well within the ten-day period mentioned on your website. I have also taken photos of the damage and the box, which I can send if needed.

I would like the store to send me a replacement lamp as soon as possible, since I need it for studying at night. If a replacement is not available, I would prefer a full refund instead.

Thank you for your help.

Sincerely,
Kenji
em-07:
Dear Mr. Okafor,

I am a second-year history student, and I am hoping you can help me with a research problem. I need the book The Silk Road Merchants by Helen Carter for my paper on trade between China and Persia in the thirteenth century. My professor specifically recommended it because it contains several primary sources that are difficult to find elsewhere.

Unfortunately, the library's only copy has been checked out for six weeks and is now overdue. According to the online catalog, it was due back eight days ago, but it still has not been returned. My paper is due in ten days, so I am running out of time.

Could you tell me what options are available to me? For example, would it be possible to request the book through interlibrary loan, or to place a recall so that it is returned sooner? If there is an electronic version or another book that covers similar material, I would also appreciate your suggestions.

Thank you very much for your time.

Sincerely,
Rebecca
em-08:
Dear Coach Henderson,

I want to apologize for arriving forty minutes late to practice last Saturday. I know it was an important session before the meet, and I understand that my lateness disrupted the relay drills for the whole team. I am truly sorry.

The mistake happened because I misread the schedule. I looked at the old version posted in the locker room in September, which listed Saturday practice at 9 a.m. instead of 8:20. I did not check the updated schedule you emailed us, and that was my responsibility.

To make sure this never happens again, I have deleted the old schedule from my phone and added every practice to my calendar with two reminders. I will also check the team email every Friday evening for any changes. In addition, I would be glad to stay after practice this week to make up the relay work I missed.

Thank you for your patience.

Sincerely,
Daniel
em-09:
Dear Dr. Kim,

I am a third-year environmental science student at Northfield University, and I am writing about my registration for the regional student conference next month. I registered through the conference website on September 2, filled in all the required information, and paid the $40 student fee by credit card.

However, I have not received a confirmation email. I have checked my spam and junk folders several times, and when I log in to the website, it does not show any record of my registration. My bank statement does show the payment, so I am unsure whether the registration was completed correctly.

Since the conference is only three weeks away and I need to book my travel and accommodation soon, could you please confirm whether I am registered? If something went wrong, I would be happy to register again or send a copy of my payment receipt.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Oliver
em-10:
Hi Leo,

It was great to hear from you, though I'm sorry you've been feeling lonely. That's completely normal when you move somewhere new. I felt exactly the same way during my first two months there, so please don't be too hard on yourself. It does get better!

There are a couple of places you should definitely check out. First, go to Harbor Market on a Saturday morning. It's full of food stalls and local musicians, and it's the perfect place to wander around. Second, try Riverside Park, which has great walking trails and a small café by the water. I used to read there every Sunday afternoon.

As for meeting people, I really recommend joining the running club that meets at the park on Wednesday evenings. Everyone is friendly, and they usually go out for pizza afterward. That's actually how I met most of my friends in the city.

Keep me updated, and call me anytime!

Take care,
Maya
em-11:
Dear Professor Moreno,

Thank you so much for taking the time to help me after class last week. I know you were busy, but you patiently went over confidence intervals with me for almost thirty minutes, and you even drew a diagram to show how sample size affects the width of an interval.

Your explanation made a real difference. Before our conversation, I could follow the formulas but did not understand what they meant. Afterward, I felt confident enough to explain the idea to my study group, and I scored 92 on the quiz, my highest grade in the course so far.

I am now considering taking your Advanced Statistics course next semester, but I am a little worried that I may not be ready. Would you recommend that I take it right away, or would it be better to wait a semester and strengthen my foundation first? If there are any topics I should review over the break, I would appreciate your suggestions.

Sincerely,
Jenna
em-12:
Dear Mr. Fischer,

I am writing about the laundry machines in the basement of our building. All three washers and both dryers have been out of order for ten days now. Each one has an "Out of Service" sign on it, but no notice has been posted explaining what happened or when they will be fixed.

This has been very inconvenient for everyone. Since I don't have a car, I have had to carry heavy bags of clothes on the bus to a laundromat across town, which takes almost three hours each time. Several neighbors, including an elderly couple on the second floor, have told me they are struggling with the same problem.

Could you please tell us when the machines are expected to be repaired? In the meantime, would it be possible to arrange a temporary solution, such as a discount at the nearest laundromat or a weekly laundry pickup service paid for by the building?

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
Adrian
em-13:
Dear Ms. Grant,

I hope you are doing well. In addition to working at the dining hall, I am a member of the student volunteer committee, which is organizing a campus food drive from November 3 to 14. Our goal is to collect 2,000 cans and boxes of non-perishable food for the Eastside Community Food Bank, which supports more than 300 local families.

Since so many students pass through the dining hall every day, it would be the perfect place to collect donations. We would like to place one large donation box near the main entrance, next to the menu board, where it would be visible but would not block the line. We would also appreciate permission to hang a small poster about the drive.

Our committee will take full responsibility for the box. Two volunteers will empty it every evening, store the donations in the student center, and deliver everything to the food bank at the end of each week.

Thank you for considering our request.

Best regards,
Nina
em-14:
Dear Mr. Nguyen,

I hope you and your family are doing well. I wanted to mention something you might not be aware of, since you are usually at work during the day. Most afternoons, from around 1 p.m. until 5 p.m., your dog Max barks quite loudly, sometimes for long stretches without stopping. I think he may just be lonely while you are away.

I study at home in the afternoons, and I have been finding it difficult to concentrate, especially now that I am preparing for my final exams. I have tried wearing headphones, but the barking still comes through clearly.

I was wondering if we could find a solution that works for both of us. Perhaps a dog walker could take Max out in the early afternoon, or he could have a few chew toys to keep him busy. If it would help, I would also be happy to walk him myself once or twice a week, since I really like him.

Thank you for understanding.

Best wishes,
Claire
em-15:
Dear Customer Support,

I am writing about an error on my bank statement. When I checked my account this week, I noticed that your fitness club charged me $45 twice on October 1. Both payments have the same description, "Monthly Membership," and they appear only a few minutes apart.

However, I have only one membership. I signed up for the Student Basic plan at your Campus Avenue location in August, and my membership number is 304-7719. The plan costs $45 per month, and I was charged correctly in previous months. I called the front desk on Monday, and the staff advised me to contact customer service by email.

Could you please look into this and refund the extra $45 to my card as soon as possible? I would also appreciate a confirmation email once the refund has been processed, as well as your assurance that the problem will not happen again next month.

Thank you for your help.

Sincerely,
Rachel
